snippet.title: I lived through the deadliest rainstorm in Egypt...and this is what it was like
snippet.description:
There was a big rain storm in Egypt this week.

In any other city, this rain storm would not have been a big deal at all. Seattle, for example, probably gets this type of rain every other day. And my home town in New Jersey gets this type of rain all the damn time.

Egypt gets practically no rain (e.g. Cairo gets on average only about 29mm of rain each year, and in many desert locations it may rain only once in several years) and so this was a HUGEEEE deal (hint: because the city is NOT equipped with a functional drainage system, power lines are all over the place, etc.).

People prepared for the rain storm like we were in for a massive Hurricane. The government basically asked the entire city to shut down for a couple days.

The whole ordeal lasted about 72 hours...and it was insane...unlike any other rain storm I have been through.

I figured it was an experience worth sharing.

Takeaway: Do not ever take a functioning sewage and drainage system for granted. They might be invisible to you on a day to day basis, but you are lucky to have them.

snippet.title: "I try to learn too many things at once"  |  How to Learn (episode #2)
snippet.description:
When asked what you struggle with when learning a new skill, many​ of you said you struggle to avoid "learning too many things at once". You know a little about a lot of things, but you never truly master any one thing.

Honestly, this is not surprising. We live in an age where we have SO much information at our fingertips. We can truly learn anything we want on the internet.  For example, I am always amazed at how much we can learn about ANYTHING on YouTube. There is literally a channel for every topic under the sun.

If you are a naturally curious person, this can be a blessing and a curse–on one hand, it is impossible to be bored because you are constantly learning random new things. But on the other hand, sticking to one subject or skill for an extended period of time feels nearly impossible and even flat out boring.

For example, how many of you found yourself in a situation where you decide you want to learn about X because it sounds really cool. You start to devour everything you can find about X. Soon enough, the initial excitement fades away and you find yourself somewhat bored or feel like you know everything you want to know about X. So you move onto the next thing (let's call this Y) and start learning all about Y. You find Y super fascinating and can't have enough of it. But eventually, Y also gets mundane and familiar. But that's okay because you are starting to find Z really interesting so you start learning about Z.

At this point, you know about X, Y, and Z on a superficial level. But you have not become truly good at any one of them. 

If this is you, you are what they call a jack(ass) of all trades. You aren't really a "jack of all trades" because to be a jack of all trades, you actually need to know each trade. Knowing a little about a lot of things makes you a jack(ass) of all trades. 

If you enjoy being a jack(ass) of all trades, then that is totally okay. But if your goal is to get really good at one thing before moving onto the next, you have no choice but to get over the constant desire to learn new things. That is what this video will help you with.

We will talk through the main reasons why you are struggling with this issue and how you can overcome it.

snippet.title: Are you struggling to learn a new skill?
snippet.description:
I launched a survey on Twitter the other day asking whether people struggle to learn new skills. Almost 50% of the people said yes (https://twitter.com/iam_preethi/status/1232771564455841794?s=20).

Honestly, I am not surprised by the results. 

I started to notice this huge gap in people's ability to learn ever since I started blogging back in 2015. The reason that many of my blogs went viral is simple: I was able to effectively teach subjects that other people struggled to learn on their own.

Sure, this was great for me because I could keep writing and making my blog get traffic. But that does not really solve the root problem, which is that people fundamentally are not being taught how to learn in school.

This has always deeply bothered me. Why? ​

Because knowing how to learn is one of the most important skills in life. It is a superpower that gives you an edge over others. It is the one and only meta-skill you need. If you know how to learn, the world is your oyster.

Achieving anything truly meaningful in life means you have to be an autodidact so that you can readily teach yourself the things you need to know.​ There simply aren't enough great teachers in the world to go around and teach everyone.

Not only that, but given the pace of innovation and change in the modern day, you have no choice but to keep learning because falling behind could mean losing your job or livelihood.

That is why I will be creating a series of videos on YouTube that teach you How to Learn. 

If you struggle to learn or simply want to become a faster/better learner, please watch this short 4 minute video.

I would love to hear from you...

What do you struggle with when you are trying to learn something. What makes you want to give up?

snippet.title: What keeps me disciplined?
snippet.description:
“How do you have so much discipline?”

I have been asked this question many times by followers and friends. To be honest, I did not realize I had discipline until people who were around me started pointing it out. It sort of grew organically because I inherently felt it was the only way to not fall prey to the modern environment.



Why am I so disciplined?


First and foremost, my discipline arises from the fact that I love and respect myself. 



This might sound cheesy but the reality is that if you truly love and respectful yourself, you are going to do the things necessary to achieve your goals and dreams. Often times, when people lack discipline, it’s not just that they lack good habits, but also that they lack self-love and self-respect. It sounds harsh, but it is the truth.

Secondly, my discipline arises from the fact that I know how to set good habits. 



People often think that they lack discipline because they lack the “motivation” to stay disciplined. Personally, I think motivation is a false God. Motivation comes and goes. You cannot rely on motivation because it is unpredictable and sporadic. 

Fundamentally, a lack of discipline is really just a lack of good habits. If you know how to set good habits, you will be disciplined. “Good” means one that you can actually stick to. Everyone knows how to set habits. Very few know how to set good habits that stick.

In this video, I share:

* What motivated me to cultivate a strong sense of discipline from a young age
* How I create habits that actually stick
* How I train my discipline (just like a muscle)

Everything in here is something you can apply and use towards your own life. I hope you find it helpful!

snippet.title: 10 things I wish I knew before starting my first startup
snippet.description:
Did you know that only 1 out of 10 startups succeed? That means 9 out of 10 of fail.

As entrepreneurs, we like to think that we are different and that our idea is awesome and that we won’t fail. I mean, I thought that too. But guess what? My first startup failed.

But that’s okay. Sometimes, failure is the only way to learn. 

In this video, I will share the top 10 things I wish I knew before starting my first tech startup. Mistakes that I want you to avoid so that you can be the 1 out of 10 that succeeds. 

If you are an entrepreneur, you probably don’t have much time to waste. So I skip all of the obvious and cliche stuff that you probably already read in business books or heard in podcasts like...

“Hire a great team”
“Talk to your users”
"Move fast and break things” 

...because you already know that stuff. 

Instead, I focus on the more nuanced mistakes that I learned the hard way.

What makes me qualified to talk about this? Good question! 

I was a founder of TruStory. We raised $3 million in seed funding from top Silicon Valley VCs. We worked relentlessly on the startup for two years. We poured our hearts and souls into it. Unfortunately, it did not work out. But I learned SO much in the process. I wouldn’t trade that experience for anything.

I now want to share my hard learned lessons with you so that you don’t waste time making the same mistakes. If you want to save months or years of time, watch till the end :) 

Is there anything you disagreed with? I’d love to hear from you in the comments!
